content.text:
Notion: Search, read, create and update pages and databases in your Notion workspace from an MCP client.
By Notion. Productivity & Projects. Verified by mcp.tc: official server from Notion.
Listing page: https://mcp.tc/i/notion
Server URL (connect to this): https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
Access: OAuth: the client opens Notion's sign-in the first time it connects.
Connects an MCP client such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex to your Notion workspace. The client can search content in Notion and connected sources, read pages, create and update content, and create pages and databases. It acts on content the signed-in user can access. Hosted by Notion as a remote server over streamable HTTP at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp, with a legacy SSE endpoint at /sse. Access uses OAuth sign-in. Workspace owners can manage MCP client access in Settings, Connections.
Setup (call get_server with client=<id> for the full steps):
- Claude Code (claude-code): `claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`
- Claude Desktop (claude-desktop): Open Customize → Connectors, click + Add, then Add custom connector, URL https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
- claude.ai (claude-ai): Add to claude.ai: https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=Notion&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.notion.com%2Fmcp
- ChatGPT (chatgpt): see client=chatgpt
- Cursor (cursor): Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=notion&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5ub3Rpb24uY29tL21jcCJ9
- VS Code (vscode): `code --add-mcp '{"name":"notion","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.notion.com/mcp"}'`
- Devin Desktop (devin): see client=devin
- Codex (codex): see client=codex
- Gemini CLI (gemini): `gemini mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`
- Any client (json): see client=json

setup.label: Claude Code
steps: Run this in a terminal, in your project folder:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
```
Start Claude Code, type `/mcp`, pick **notion** and choose **Authenticate**. A browser window opens for the Notion sign-in.
setup.code: claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
setup.note: Add `--scope user` to make it available in every project, not just this one.

setup.label: Claude Desktop
setup.quick: Open Customize → Connectors, click + Add, then Add custom connector, URL https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
steps: Open **Customize → Connectors**, click **+ Add**, then **Add custom connector**.
Name it **Notion** and paste this URL:
https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
Click **Add**, then **Connect**, and sign in when Notion asks.
setup.note: Claude Desktop’s JSON config file only starts local servers. Remote servers go through Connectors, and connectors you add on claude.ai show up here too.

setup.label: claude.ai
steps: Open the connector form on claude.ai. This button fills in the name and URL for you:
Add to claude.ai: https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=Notion&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.notion.com%2Fmcp
Check that the URL reads `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp` and click **Add**.
Click **Connect** and sign in when Notion asks.
setup.note: Free plans allow one custom connector. On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds it under **Organization settings → Connectors**.

setup.label: ChatGPT
steps: On chatgpt.com, open **Settings → Security and login** and turn on **Developer mode**.
Go to `chatgpt.com/plugins` and click **+** to create an app for a remote MCP server.
Paste `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp` as the server URL and choose **OAuth**. ChatGPT sends you to Notion to sign in.
setup.note: Developer mode is available on the web for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education accounts.

setup.label: Cursor
steps: Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=notion&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5ub3Rpb24uY29tL21jcCJ9
Or add it by hand to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (this project):
setup.note: Cursor shows **Needs authentication** next to the server. Click the button beside it to sign in.

setup.label: VS Code
steps: Install in VS Code: https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=notion&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.notion.com%2Fmcp%22%7D
Or from a terminal:

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"notion","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.notion.com/mcp"}'
```
Or commit it to the repo in `.vscode/mcp.json`:
setup.note: VS Code asks you to sign in the first time the server starts.

setup.label: Devin Desktop
steps: Add it to `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` (macOS and Linux) or `%APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json` (Windows):
Refresh the MCP server list in Cascade and sign in when asked.
setup.note: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf. It reads `serverUrl` (or `url`) for remote servers.

setup.label: Codex
steps:
```bash
codex mcp add notion --url https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
codex mcp login notion
```
Or edit `~/.codex/config.toml` directly:

```toml
[mcp_servers.notion]
url = "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp"
```
setup.code:
codex mcp add notion --url https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
codex mcp login notion

setup.label: Gemini CLI
steps:
```bash
gemini mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
```
Then, inside Gemini CLI, run `/mcp auth notion` to sign in.
setup.code: gemini mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
setup.note: This adds it to the current project. Add `-s user` to use it everywhere.

setup.label: Any client
steps: Most clients accept this shape. Some name the URL field differently: `serverUrl` in Devin Desktop, `httpUrl` in Gemini CLI’s settings file.
Zed puts servers under `context_servers` in its settings. Cline needs `"type": "streamableHttp"`, or it assumes SSE.
Client only starts local servers? Bridge it with `npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`.
